note: Adapted from Emerson's (1928) species description, originally in English; the species was published under the old combination Termes (Termes) schmitzi and is now placed in Odontotermes (Species File: Odontotermes schmitzi (Emerson, 1928)), and the type locality Stanleyville agrees with the checklist. The holotype is an alate and the morphotype a soldier; the description is based on several alates and soldiers, one queen (No. 25T) and several workers, the workers not being described separately. Type locality: the Stanleyville area, Belgian Congo (collected by Kohl, No. 22T); another locality: near Lukolela (collected by Lang-Chapin, 17/7/1909). The species is named after the Jesuit father H. Schmitz. The original also gives a set of queen measurements (body length 75.00 mm, abdominal width 18.00 mm), which have been merged into the alate section. OCR problems: the length with wings read "25 00-26.00" (the decimal point read as a space) and the hind tibia "2 . 71- 2.80", restored here according to the values; the synonymy citations, the figure numbers and the parts of the comparison section that do not concern this species have not been translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate compared with T. latialatus, the latter having the notch of the anterior pronotal margin almost indiscernible and the pronotum wider; T. buchholzi and T. agilis are larger; the pronotum of T. salebrifrons is about as wide as the head between the compound eyes; the ocelli of T. culturarum are farther from the eyes; the pronotum of T. amanicus is larger. Soldier compared with T. culturarum, which is smaller; the T. badius of Natal (1894, collected by Haviland) has proportionally longer mandibles, a shorter head and sides more distinctly narrowed anteriorly; the head of T. monodon is proportionally wider; T. amanicus is closely related but has a more distinct cephalic carina.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown, oval, densely covered with long hairs. Fontanelle a small point at the middle of the frons. Antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 slightly smaller than segment 4, segment 4 shorter than segment 2. Compound eyes rather large, rather close to the lower margin of the head. Ocelli large in the male, less than their width from the eye; smaller in the female, about their width from the eye. Labrum with a pale transverse band. Postclypeus far less than half as long as wide, the median longitudinal line visible. Pronotum nearly concolorous with the head; the sides strongly contracted posteriorly, the corners rounded; the posterior margin slightly concave, the anterior margin concave. Posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum broadly concave, the corners rounded. Wings yellowish brown. Measurements (mm): length with wings 25.00—26.00, length without wings 11.00—12.00, head length 2.89—3.06, head width 2.62—2.71, eye diameter 0.73—0.74, pronotal length 1.09—1.23, pronotal width 2.23—2.36, hind tibia length 2.71—2.80, forewing length 21.00—22.00, forewing width 5.50—5.60; queen body length 75.00, queen abdominal width 18.00.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head red-yellow; the sides slightly rounded, narrowing anteriorly; the head surface with a few scattered setae. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 smaller than segment 2, segment 4 as long as segment 2. A black eye spot behind the antennal base. Mandibles black except at the base. Anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum both concave. Measurements (mm): head length 5.25—5.68, head width 2.89—3.23, antennal length 2.62—2.89, pronotal length 0.87—1.05, pronotal width 1.95—2.01, hind tibia length 2.27—2.45, left mandible length 1.66—1.92.
